canonical_updates.content:
# P1 Databricks Workload

## Purpose and scope

P1 ingests JSON events from Kafka into a bronze Delta table, quarantines invalid messages, and maintains the latest valid event per `event_key` in silver. Gold transformations are out of scope.

## Architecture and contracts

- `jobs/P1/` contains the authoritative Databricks Declarative Automation Bundle. The daily job runs bronze first and silver only after bronze succeeds; both tasks receive the same `environment` parameter.
- `notebooks/P1/bronze/bronze_ingestion.py` reads `my-topic` incrementally using Structured Streaming `AvailableNow`, persists progress in `{data_path}/checkpoints/P1/bronze_ingestion`, and idempotently writes source records keyed by `(topic, partition, offset)` to `<database>.p1_test_kfk_brz`.
- Bronze Change Data Feed is enabled for silver consumption. `notebooks/P1/silver/silver_processing.py` reads CDF using `AvailableNow` and its stable checkpoint `{data_path}/checkpoints/P1/silver_processing`.
- Silver writes the latest valid event for each nonblank `event_key` to `<database>.p1_test`, preserving other JSON properties in a `VARIANT` attributes column. It writes malformed JSON, non-object roots, and invalid keys to `<database>.p1_test_kfk_quarantine` with source metadata and diagnostics.
- Latest-event ordering is source timestamp, then Kafka partition and offset. Silver and quarantine writes are independently idempotent Delta operations; they are not a cross-table transaction.
- The project requires Databricks Runtime 15.4 LTS or later for the silver `VARIANT` behavior.

## Configuration and security

`configs/{environment}.yaml` supplies environment-specific settings. The current `prod.yaml` has database `test_prod`, data path `s3://test_prod`, Kafka host `test.com:9995`, topic `my-topic`, and secret key name `my-secret`. Kafka username and Databricks secret scope are unset deployment inputs. Password material belongs only in Databricks Secrets. Never use production to test this workload.

The `prod` bundle target also requires deployment-provided schedule/timezone, compute policy/runtime, run-as service principal, and retry values. Required permissions include Kafka topic and secret access, checkpoint/storage access, bronze CDF reads, and silver/quarantine writes.

## Verification and release status

The user accepted a verification waiver because no Databricks environment is available. Python syntax checks and static Bundle source checks passed; the current 16-test suite covers AI-DLC lifecycle tooling only. P1 Kafka/Spark/Delta runtime behavior, performance, authenticated Bundle validation, and production permissions remain unverified. No job has been deployed and no notebook or production data has been run. The waiver is not evidence of runtime success or production readiness.

Before a release, supply deployment values through the approved non-secret mechanism, validate the Bundle in an authorized workspace, and run P1 integration and performance checks in an isolated non-production Databricks environment. Operations procedures for monitoring, alerting, incidents, rollback, maintenance, and on-call ownership still need to be defined.

# AI-DLC Intent Lifecycle

The project AI-DLC workflow is defined in `.agents/skills/aidlc-workflows/`. `aidlc-docs/aidlc-state.md` is the current intent state record; `aidlc-docs/audit.md` records active history. Closed intent summaries and full snapshots are stored in `aidlc-docs/archive/<intent-id>/`.

The lifecycle supports `ACTIVE`, `VERIFICATION_COMPLETE`, `VERIFICATION_WAIVED`, `COMPACTION`, `COMPACTION_FAILED`, `COMPACTED`, and `CLOSED`. `VERIFICATION_COMPLETE` requires successful Build and Test verification and approval. `VERIFICATION_WAIVED` requires explicit user acceptance of a documented limitation; it must never be reported as a passing result.

After a passed result or accepted waiver and separate approval to close, prepare a curated manifest at `aidlc-docs/compaction/<intent-id>/manifest.json`. A waiver manifest uses `verification.status: waived`, `verification.user_accepted: true`, and details describing the unverified scope; the lifecycle state must record the same accepted waiver. Run a dry-run and review its archive, canonical updates, and cleanup list before applying.

Use `python3 scripts/aidlc_intent.py compact <intent-id> --dry-run` to preview and `python3 scripts/aidlc_intent.py compact <intent-id> --apply` to archive the complete listed history, apply curated canonical updates, clear workflow-only inception/construction artifacts, and close the intent. Never put application source or configuration in cleanup paths. Runtime waivers do not authorize deployment.
